question: Should OpenClaw retire the built-in plugin dependency denylist and rely on ClawHub, security.installPolicy, and before_install hooks for dependency package-name blocks?
rationale: This changes the default install security boundary and reverses the denylist-preservation choice from the earlier operator-policy PR, so automation cannot decide it from tests alone.

options.title: Accept denylist retirement
options.body: Merge after owners accept that hard-coded package-name blocks are retired and that ClawHub/operator policy/hooks own this trust boundary.

options.title: Keep built-in package blocks
options.body: Require the PR to preserve or replace the current denylist behavior until a maintainer-approved migration or replacement policy exists.

options.title: Defer for security owner review
options.body: Leave the draft open until the install-security owner decides whether plain package-name blocking still belongs in core.

recommendation.title: Accept denylist retirement
recommendation.body: Merge after owners accept that hard-coded package-name blocks are retired and that ClawHub/operator policy/hooks own this trust boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: jesse-merhi owns this PR and has recent merged ClawHub trust-boundary work connected to the proposed replacement trust model.
